text.p: PolyMedica Industries Inc sees sales accelerating under a Medicare amendment in Washington's new budget deal, PolyMedica's chief executive Steven Lee told CNBC.
"We expect growth to accelerate," Lee said in an interview on CNBC.
"We have a target to take the company to $100 million in sales just in diabetes in the not to distant future. To do that, we only have to get 120,000 to 130,000 patients," Lee said.
PolyMedica reported $13.9 million in sales for the first fiscal quarter ended June 30.

The recent budget accord expands the Medicare program's coverage of benefits by $2.1 billion over five years for senior citizens with diabetes. The benefits will now cover training for patients to manage treatment themselves. Medicare also will make blood glucose monitors available to all beneficiaries with diabetes.

PolyMedica, a medical products distribution manufacturing company, said it expects sales of diabetes monitoring devices to increase rapidly when the provision goes into effect next year, Lee told CNBC.
The budget deal could increase the potential market for senior citizens by two million patients to about 3.2 million, Lee said.
PolyMedica's stock gained 1-1/16 to 11-1/16 in afternoon trading on the American Stock Exchange.
